ROLE: reporter
You write the final diagnosis of an incident from the evidence gathered. Every statement must be backed by evidence IDs taken from the evidence list; never invent an ID.

Root-cause categories (root_cause_category must be exactly one of these):
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Rules:
- claims: factual statements about what the evidence shows. Each cites one or more evidence IDs (log lines L-..., metrics M-..., runbook sections R-...) that actually support it.
- recommended_actions: concrete next steps for the on-call engineer, taken from the retrieved runbook sections. Each cites at least one runbook section ID (R-...).
- ruled_out: other hypotheses you considered and rejected, as short strings.
- confidence: low, medium or high.

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"incident_id": "INC-029", "root_cause_category": "disk_full", "root_cause_summary": "one or two sentences", "confidence": "high", "claims": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["L-0123", "M-021"]}], "recommended_actions": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["R-06-5"]}], "ruled_out": ["..."]}

Alert: auth-service: HTTP error rate above 5% for 5 minutes (since 11:42 UTC)
Alerting service: auth
Alert time: 2026-05-08T11:42:00Z
Data available from 2026-05-08T10:00:00Z to 2026-05-08T13:00:00Z

Evidence:
Step 1: metrics_query {"end": "2026-05-08T12:00:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "auth", "start": "2026-05-08T11:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check error rate metrics for auth service around the alert time.)
  Result: M-005: Change detected at 2026-05-08T11:40:00Z: mean 0.36 before, 15.91 after (124.8 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-005] auth.error_rate_pct from 2026-05-08T11:00:00Z to 2026-05-08T12:00:00Z (13 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.1 max=16.09 mean=6.34 last=15.83; mean=6.34. Change detected at 2026-05-08T11:40:00Z: mean 0.36 before, 15.91 after (124.8 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-05-08T11:10:00Z = 0.1 (lowest); 2026-05-08T11:40:00Z = 15.86 (first point after the change); 2026-05-08T11:45:00Z = 16.09 (peak); 2026-05-08T12:00:00Z = 15.83 (last).
Step 2: metrics_query {"end": "2026-05-08T12:00:00Z", "metric": "cpu_pct", "service": "auth", "start": "2026-05-08T11:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check CPU usage for auth service around the alert time.)
  Result: M-002: Change detected at 2026-05-08T11:15:00Z: mean 37.44 before, 62.25 after (21.4 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-002] auth.cpu_pct from 2026-05-08T11:00:00Z to 2026-05-08T12:00:00Z (13 points, 5-minute steps): min=35.17 max=99.49 mean=56.53 last=97.52; mean=56.53. Change detected at 2026-05-08T11:15:00Z: mean 37.44 before, 62.25 after (21.4 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-05-08T11:15:00Z = 43.36 (first point after the change); 2026-05-08T11:20:00Z = 35.17 (lowest); 2026-05-08T11:50:00Z = 99.49 (peak); 2026-05-08T12:00:00Z = 97.52 (last).
Step 3: metrics_query {"end": "2026-05-08T12:00:00Z", "metric": "request_rate_rps", "service": "auth", "start": "2026-05-08T11:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if request rate increased to see if this is a traffic spike.)
  Result: M-008: Change detected at 2026-05-08T11:40:00Z: mean 452.67 before, 1800.42 after (161.0 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-008] auth.request_rate_rps from 2026-05-08T11:00:00Z to 2026-05-08T12:00:00Z (13 points, 5-minute steps): min=441.11 max=1813.3 mean=971.04 last=1802.29; mean=971.04. Change detected at 2026-05-08T11:40:00Z: mean 452.67 before, 1800.42 after (161.0 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-05-08T11:10:00Z = 441.11 (lowest); 2026-05-08T11:40:00Z = 1813.3 (first point after the change); 2026-05-08T11:40:00Z = 1813.3 (peak); 2026-05-08T12:00:00Z = 1802.29 (last).
Step 4: metrics_query {"end": "2026-05-08T12:00:00Z", "metric": "restarts", "service": "auth", "start": "2026-05-08T11:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if container restarts occurred around the time of the error spike.)
  Result: M-009: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-009] auth.restarts from 2026-05-08T11:00:00Z to 2026-05-08T12:00:00Z (13 points, 5-minute steps): min=0 max=0 mean=0 last=0; mean=0. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-05-08T11:00:00Z = 0 (lowest); 2026-05-08T11:00:00Z = 0 (peak); 2026-05-08T12:00:00Z = 0 (last).
Step 5: log_search {"end": "2026-05-08T12:00:00Z", "level": "ERROR", "query": "deploy, error, exception, OOM", "service": "auth", "start": "2026-05-08T11:30:00Z"} (asked because: Search error logs in auth service around the incident start time for clues on root cause.)
  Result: 0 matching log lines.

Hypotheses from the investigation:
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: A huge increase in request rate (from ~450 to ~1800 RPS) started at 11:40 UTC, directly matching the sudden increase in error rates and high CPU utilization. (evidence: M-005, M-002, M-008)
- bad_deployment: Errors and CPU spiked around the same time as the traffic increase, but a software defect triggered under high load or around this time cannot be completely ruled out yet. (evidence: M-005, M-002, M-008)
- memory_leak_oom: CPU usage is elevated, but container restarts remain at zero, making memory leak/OOM less likely. (evidence: M-002, M-009)

Your previous diagnosis was rejected for these problems. Fix them and reply with the corrected JSON:
- claim 4 ('Container restarts remained at zero throughout the entire incident win...') is not supported by the evidence it cites (M-009): only 7% of its key terms appear there. Cite evidence that states it, or rewrite or remove the claim.
- There are no recommended actions, and no runbook section was retrieved to cite.
